title: Cooldown 還是 phased rollout——兩種對抗供應鏈攻擊的提案
summary: Cooldown 對小套件統計上不公平、攻擊窗口被打平卻沒消失——phased rollout 把 canary 風險按下游影響規模分階段曝光,是更可審計的替代設計。
widget_questions: Across seven dimensions (small-package fairness, attack window, transitive coverage, signal quality, opt-in defaults, maintainer overhead, enterprise granularity), where does each approach win?
How does cooldown effectiveness degrade as package popularity decreases, and how does phased rollout flatten that disparity across download-rank strata?
What do the cliff edge (cooldown) and the 14-step staircase (phased rollout) look like side-by-side as static shapes, and why does the cliff create a 'detection desert' that the staircase doesn't?
How do the cumulative downstream-adoption curves differ between a 3-day cooldown (cliff edge) and a 14-day phased rollout (linear ramp), and where is the exploitable attack window largest under each?
For three real 2026 supply-chain incidents (LiteLLM, Nx, axios), which approach would have contained the blast radius, and which approach merely shifted the canary burden onto someone else?
Which cooldown flag, default N, and transitive-coverage policy does each of the four major package managers (npm, pnpm, pip, uv) ship as of 2026-05, and how aligned are they on a single value?

Which consumer class (solo dev, SaaS production, enterprise staging, finance/health production, lockfile-frozen transitive) naturally maps onto which phased-rollout stage, and what does cooldown lose by collapsing all of these into one N?
